messages.text: Payment API is returning HTTP 500 errors in production. Multiple customers unable to complete transactions.
Checking logs now. Seeing a lot of connection timeout errors in the payment-service pod logs.
Database monitoring shows active connections at 50/50. Pool is completely exhausted.
Maximum DB connections is currently configured to 50. That was set during initial deployment and never adjusted.
Traffic has increased 3x since last month. 50 connections is clearly insufficient now.
Increasing the pool size to 100 and restarting payment-service. Applying config change now.
Service is stable now. Error rate has returned to normal. Active connections at 35/100.
Resolved. Root cause was DB connection pool exhaustion due to increased traffic without capacity adjustment.
Order Service is throwing HTTP 503 Service Unavailable errors. Customers seeing failures at checkout.
Kubernetes dashboard shows order-service pods are in CrashLoopBackOff. Only 1 of 5 replicas running.
Pod logs show OOMKilled. Memory usage spiking to 2GB before kill. Current limit is 2Gi.
Found the issue. Yesterday's deployment added a new caching layer that loads all product catalog into memory on startup.
Product catalog is 1.8GB now. That plus JVM overhead exceeds the 2GB limit.
Rolling back the caching change and increasing memory limit to 4Gi as temporary fix.
All pods back to Running state. Order processing has resumed. Error rate at 0%.
Root cause: Memory exhaustion caused by loading full product catalog into in-memory cache without size limits. Rolling back deployment resolved it.
Authentication Service is rejecting all login requests. Users getting 401 Unauthorized across all applications.
Checking auth-service logs. Seeing 'JWT verification failed: certificate expired' errors.
The signing certificate shows expiry date of 2026-08-02. It expired yesterday!
We need to generate a new certificate and update it in the secrets. No auto-rotation was configured.
Generated new cert with 1-year validity. Updating Kubernetes secret now.
Secret updated. Restarting auth-service pods to pick up new cert.
Login working again across all services. Confirmed with multiple test accounts.
Resolved. Root cause was expired JWT signing certificate. No auto-renewal was configured. Adding cert-manager rotation as follow-up task.
Notification Service is not sending any emails or SMS. No errors in dashboard but users are not receiving OTPs.
Checking Kafka consumer group. Notification-consumer shows lag of 50,000 messages and increasing.
Consumer instances show they're connected but not processing. All in rebalancing state.
Found it. Last deploy changed the consumer group ID. The new group started from latest offset, missing all pending messages. Also, session timeout is too low causing constant rebalancing.
Reverting consumer group ID to original and increasing session.timeout.ms from 10000 to 30000.
Consumer is processing again. Lag dropping rapidly. OTP messages being delivered now.
Resolved. Root cause: Kafka consumer group ID changed in deployment causing consumer rebalancing loop. Reverting group ID and increasing session timeout fixed it.
Customer Service API response times have gone from 200ms to 15 seconds. Multiple timeout errors from upstream services.
Database query analysis shows a specific query taking 12 seconds. It's the customer search query with LIKE '%pattern%'.
Checking pg_locks. There are 8 blocked transactions waiting. Two long-running transactions holding row locks.
Found the deadlock. A batch update job and the API are both trying to acquire locks on the same rows in opposite order.
Killing the batch job process. We need to add proper lock ordering to prevent this.
Batch job killed. Blocked transactions released. Response times back to normal 200ms.
Resolved. Root cause: Database deadlock between batch update job and API requests. Inconsistent lock ordering caused mutual blocking. Fixed by terminating batch job. Need to redesign lock strategy.
Inventory Service is returning stale data. Stock counts don't match warehouse system. Customers ordering out-of-stock items.
Redis cache shows inventory data with TTL of -1. Data was cached but never being refreshed.
The cache invalidation worker connects to Redis cluster. Connection logs show 'READONLY You can not write against a read only replica'.
Redis failover happened yesterday. The worker is still connected to the old master which is now a replica. No auto-reconnect configured.
Restarting the cache invalidation worker. Also enabling Redis Sentinel support so it auto-discovers the new master.
Worker restarted and connected to correct master. Cache flushed and repopulating with fresh data.
Resolved. Root cause: Redis connection failure after failover. Cache invalidation worker was connected to old master (now replica). Fixed by restarting worker and enabling Sentinel-aware connections.
Loan Service approval workflow is failing. All loan applications stuck in PENDING state for the last 2 hours.
Checking the external credit scoring API integration. Getting connection timeout errors to credit-bureau.example.com.
DNS resolution for credit-bureau.example.com is failing. nslookup returns SERVFAIL.
Our CoreDNS pods are running but the upstream forwarder was changed in yesterday's infra update. It's pointing to a decommissioned DNS server.
Updating CoreDNS ConfigMap to point to the correct upstream DNS servers. Restarting CoreDNS pods.
DNS resolution working now. Loan service can reach credit bureau again. Stuck applications are being processed.
Resolved. Root cause: DNS resolution failure due to CoreDNS upstream forwarder pointing to decommissioned server after infra update. Fixed by correcting DNS configuration.
Reporting Service dashboard is completely unresponsive. HTTP 500 on all report generation endpoints.
Application logs show 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space' repeatedly.
Heap dump analysis shows 80% of memory consumed by a single ArrayList holding 5 million report rows.
The monthly report endpoint loads all data into memory before pagination. No streaming or chunking.
Quick fix: increasing JVM heap from 2G to 8G and adding -XX:+UseG1GC. Long-term fix needs streaming implementation.
Deployed with increased heap. Reports generating again. Will create ticket for streaming refactor.
Resolved. Root cause: Memory exhaustion in Reporting Service due to loading entire dataset into memory for monthly report. Temporary fix: increased heap size. Permanent fix: implement data streaming.
Payment API returning HTTP 500 again. This is the third time this month. Customers complaining on social media.
Different root cause this time. Not connection pool. Seeing 'Connection refused' to payment-gateway downstream service.
Payment gateway pods are running but not ready. Readiness probe failing with 'TLS handshake timeout'.
The payment gateway's TLS certificate was renewed yesterday but the new cert has a different CN. Our service is rejecting it due to hostname verification.
Updating the trust store with the new certificate and the expected CN in our configuration.
Configuration updated and service restarted. TLS handshake succeeding now. Payments flowing.
Resolved. Root cause: Downstream payment gateway renewed TLS cert with different CN. Our hostname verification failed. Fixed by updating trust store and CN configuration.
Order Service is extremely slow. P99 latency jumped from 500ms to 30 seconds. No errors but everything is timing out.
CPU usage on order-service pods is at 98%. All 4 pods are maxed out.
Thread dump shows 200 threads stuck in a regex pattern matching loop. The new input validation regex is catastrophic.
Identified the regex: ^(a+)+$ in the order validation code deployed this morning. Classic ReDoS pattern.
Rolling back to previous deployment version. HPA is not helping because CPU is stuck in regex execution, not actual load.
Rollback complete. CPU back to normal 15%. Latency returned to 500ms P99.
Resolved. Root cause: CPU spike caused by catastrophic backtracking in regex validation (ReDoS). Rolled back deployment. Need to fix regex before redeploying.
Authentication Service returning 503. This is different from last week's cert issue. Service is up but overloaded.
Rate limiting is kicking in. Someone is hammering the login endpoint. 50,000 requests per minute from a single IP range.
Looks like a brute force attack. All requests targeting the /auth/login endpoint with different username/password combinations.
Adding WAF rule to block the IP range 103.45.x.x. Also increasing rate limit threshold and enabling CAPTCHA after 5 failed attempts.
WAF rule applied. Attack traffic blocked. Legitimate traffic flowing normally. No accounts compromised based on audit log.
Resolved. Root cause: Authentication Service overloaded by brute force login attack from single IP range. Fixed by blocking attacker IPs via WAF and enhancing rate limiting.
Inventory Service sync job failing. New stock updates from warehouse not reflecting in the system since last night.
The sync job connects to warehouse API. Logs show HTTP 401 Unauthorized from warehouse endpoint.
API key for warehouse integration was rotated by their team yesterday. We were notified but the ticket was missed.
Got the new API key from warehouse team. Updating the secret in vault and restarting sync job.
Sync job running successfully now. Backlog of 500 inventory updates being processed. Should be caught up in 10 minutes.
Resolved. Root cause: Warehouse API key rotation without updating our configuration. Authentication failure on downstream API. Fixed by updating API key in vault.
Payment API returning HTTP 500 errors. Third incident on payment this week. Checking if it's the same DB pool issue.
DB connection pool is fine at 45/100. This is something else. Error logs show 'Deadlock detected' on the transactions table.
Two concurrent payment retries are updating the same transaction row. The retry logic doesn't acquire an advisory lock.
The payment retry worker was deployed with parallel processing yesterday. Previous version was single-threaded so deadlocks were impossible.
Adding SELECT FOR UPDATE NOWAIT before the payment update. Also reducing retry parallelism to 2 workers temporarily.
Fix deployed. No more deadlocks in the last 10 minutes. Payment success rate back to 99.9%.
Resolved. Root cause: Database deadlock in payment transactions caused by parallel retry workers without proper lock ordering. Fixed with SELECT FOR UPDATE NOWAIT and reduced parallelism.
Notification Service email delivery rate dropped to 0%. SMS still working. No errors in our logs.
SMTP connection to our email provider is succeeding but emails are being silently dropped. Checking provider dashboard.
Email provider shows our sending domain SPF record is invalid. Someone modified our DNS TXT records yesterday during the zone migration.
Confirmed. The SPF TXT record was truncated during migration. Provider is rejecting all emails due to SPF fail.
Restoring the correct SPF record in Route53. TTL is 300 seconds so should propagate quickly.
SPF record propagated. Email provider confirming deliveries are going through again. Backlog being processed.
Resolved. Root cause: DNS configuration issue - SPF TXT record was corrupted during zone migration causing email provider to reject all outgoing emails. Fixed by restoring correct SPF record.
Loan Service is returning HTTP 500 on new loan application submissions. Existing loans unaffected.
Error trace shows NullPointerException in the loan eligibility calculator. Stack trace points to the new credit tier logic.
The new deployment added a credit_tier field that's required by the calculator but the database migration hasn't run yet. Field is NULL for all records.
Classic deployment ordering issue. Code was deployed before the migration. Running migration now with default value of 'STANDARD'.
Migration complete. All existing records now have credit_tier = 'STANDARD'. New submissions working.
Resolved. Root cause: Deployment configuration issue - application code deployed before database migration. New required field was NULL causing NullPointerException. Fixed by running migration.
